pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these gases do we breathe in to stay alive? (1 mark)
   A. Smoke
   B. Oxygen
   C. Dust
   D. Petrol fumes

2. Which of these is true of a gas? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot spread out
   B. It is always visible
   C. It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume
   D. It keeps its own shape

3. Why is air matter? (1 mark)
   A. It is invisible
   B. It is light
   C. It has mass and takes up space
   D. It is cold

4. A jug has 400 ml of water. Fatuma adds 250 ml. How much water is in the jug? (1 mark)
   A. 150 ml
   B. 450 ml
   C. 600 ml
   D. 650 ml

5. In the dry tissue experiment, why does the tissue stay dry? (1 mark)
   A. Air in the cup keeps the water out
   B. Water cannot touch paper
   C. The cup is made of plastic
   D. The tissue is warm

6. Which of these is heavier: 3 kg of sugar or 3000 g of sugar? (1 mark)
   A. 3000 g
   B. Cannot tell
   C. They have the same mass
   D. 3 kg

7. Which of these can be poured and takes the shape of its container? (1 mark)
   A. Brick
   B. Stone
   C. Water
   D. Book

8. How many millilitres are in 1 litre? (1 mark)
   A. 100
   B. 10 000
   C. 1000
   D. 10

9. Which of these is a tool for picking up waste safely? (1 mark)
   A. Bare hands
   B. A rake
   C. Bare feet
   D. A towel

10. Why should waste bins have lids? (1 mark)
   A. To make them look nice
   B. To keep out flies and rats
   C. To make waste heavier
   D. To make waste rot faster

11. Which is the best order of managing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Recycle, reuse, reduce
   B. Burn, bury, throw
   C. Reduce, reuse, recycle
   D. Throw, burn, bury

12. Which of these is non-decomposable? (1 mark)
   A. Fruit peel
   B. Dry leaves
   C. Dung
   D. Plastic bottle

13. Why is burning plastic bad? (1 mark)
   A. It makes rain
   B. It makes harmful smoke
   C. It is safe for everyone
   D. It makes good manure

14. Which item can be reused as a toy wheel? (1 mark)
   A. Banana peel
   B. Bottle tops
   C. Leaves
   D. Ash

15. Which waste can be reused as a pencil holder? (1 mark)
   A. Banana peel
   B. Egg shells
   C. Old leaves
   D. An empty tin

16. Why must we conserve water? (1 mark)
   A. Fresh water is limited
   B. Water is always free
   C. Water is not needed
   D. Water never ends

17. A leaking pipe wastes 5 litres each day. How much is wasted in 7 days? (1 mark)
   A. 70 litres
   B. 35 litres
   C. 57 litres
   D. 12 litres

18. What is mulching? (1 mark)
   A. Digging deep holes
   B. Removing all plants
   C. Burning grass
   D. Covering soil with dry grass or leaves

19. Why should a rainwater tank be covered? (1 mark)
   A. To make it rain
   B. To make water heavier
   C. To keep out mosquitoes and dirt
   D. To keep the water warm

20. Which of these is an example of a place where water may be recycled? (1 mark)
   A. A dry shamba
   B. A tap
   C. A water treatment plant
   D. A road

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give three ways of saving water at home. (3 marks)

22. Describe how you would make a dustbin from locally available materials. (4 marks)

23. Describe how rainwater can be harvested from a school roof. (3 marks)

24. Explain the difference between reusing and recycling. (3 marks)

25. A shopkeeper has 2 kg of sugar and 750 g of salt. Find the total mass in grams. (3 marks)

26. Describe how solid waste causes flooding in towns. (4 marks)

27. Name the three states of matter and give one example of each. (2 marks)

28. State two reasons for conserving water. (2 marks)

29. Explain why a rainwater tank should have a lid. (3 marks)

30. Give three ways of protecting water sources. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Oxygen
   Oxygen in the air is needed for life.

2. C — It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume
   A gas spreads to fill the space.

3. C — It has mass and takes up space
   Air fills balloons and pushes against things, so it takes up space.

4. D — 650 ml
   400 + 250 = 650 ml.

5. A — Air in the cup keeps the water out
   Air takes up the space inside the cup.

6. C — They have the same mass
   3 kg equals 3000 g.

7. C — Water
   Water is a liquid.

8. C — 1000
   1 litre is 1000 ml.

9. B — A rake
   A rake or shovel keeps hands away from the waste.

10. B — To keep out flies and rats
   Covered bins reduce smell and pests.

11. C — Reduce, reuse, recycle
   First make less waste, then reuse, then recycle.

12. D — Plastic bottle
   Plastic does not rot easily.

13. B — It makes harmful smoke
   Burning plastic gives off harmful smoke.

14. B — Bottle tops
   Bottle tops make good wheels for toys.

15. D — An empty tin
   A clean tin can be reused.

16. A — Fresh water is limited
   Only a small part of the world's water is fresh and usable.

17. B — 35 litres
   5 x 7 = 35 litres.

18. D — Covering soil with dry grass or leaves
   Mulch reduces evaporation from the soil.

19. C — To keep out mosquitoes and dirt
   A cover stops mosquitoes breeding and dirt getting in.

20. C — A water treatment plant
   Treatment plants clean used water.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Close taps, use a cup or basin, fix leaks, use a bucket instead of a hose, reuse washing water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a strong bucket, box or container. Cut and smooth the top and cover any sharp edge. Make a lid if possible. Paint a label saying waste only and put it in a suitable place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain falls on the roof and runs into the gutter. The gutter leads to a pipe which fills a covered tank.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for roof and gutter, 1 mark for pipe, 1 mark for tank.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Reusing means using an item again in the same or a new way without changing it, for example a bottle for water. Recycling means turning waste into a new product, for example melting old plastic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reuse, 1 mark for recycle, 1 mark for one example.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2750 g.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 2 kg = 2000 g, 1 mark for adding 750 g and 1 mark for the answer.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Polythene bags and plastic block drains. Water cannot flow away when it rains. It gathers in the streets and floods homes and roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 4.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Solid (stone), liquid (water), gas (air).
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for the three states and 1 mark for correct examples.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: To have enough water for all, to save money, for crops and animals, to protect sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps out dirt and leaves and stops mosquitoes from breeding in it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for mosquitoes, 1 mark for making water safer.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plant trees near rivers, do not throw waste in water, do not wash in springs, keep animals away from drinking sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
